title: MCP update_set clears collection_id, so the set drops out of its collection
body:
## Summary

Calling the MCP `update_set` tool to change a set's name or description also clears the set's `collection_id`. The set drops out of its collection and no longer shows in the collection's set and view counts. Nothing in the tool's response warns about it.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Take a set that belongs to a collection.
2. Call `update_set` with only `set_id` and a new `description`.
3. Read the response, or `get_set` the set.

## Expected

The description changes. `collection_id` is unchanged.

## Actual

The response shows `"collection_id": null` and `"collection_name": null`. The set is now ungrouped, so the collection lists one set fewer and its views disappear from the collection's view count.

A follow-on error shows up if the collection's thumbnail diagram lives in that set. The next `update_collection` call fails with HTTP 400, "Thumbnail diagram does not belong to a set in this collection".

This happened twice in one working session, each time after a plain description edit.

## Root cause

The MCP handler and the backend disagree on what a missing field means.

- `mcp/src/iris_mcp/tools.py:941` builds `_SET_METADATA_FIELDS` by removing `collection_id` from `_SET_UPDATE_FIELDS`, so that moves go through `move_set`.
- `_update_set` (`tools.py:962`) passes `_SET_METADATA_FIELDS` to `_put_merge_partial`. That merge only copies the fields it is given, so the PUT body has no `collection_id` at all.
- `backend/app/sets/models.py:43` defaults `SetUpdate.collection_id` to `None`, and `backend/app/sets/service.py:296-314` always writes `collection_id = ?`. A missing field becomes `NULL`.

The frontend set page is not affected, because it always sends `collection_id` (`frontend/src/routes/sets/[id]/+page.svelte:108`).

The existing test hides the bug. `mcp/tests/test_update_tools.py:104` (`TestUpdateSet`) asserts that `collection_id` is not in the PUT body (line 131), and the mocked PUT response returns `collection_id="col-7"`. So the test passes while the real backend un-groups the set.

## Suggested fix

1. **MCP (smallest fix).** In `_update_set`, keep `collection_id` out of the tool's input schema but carry the current value through the merge. `_move_set` (`tools.py:1122`) already does this. For example, merge with `_SET_UPDATE_FIELDS` and drop any caller-supplied `collection_id` first.
2. **Backend (defence in depth).** Treat an omitted `collection_id` as "leave unchanged". Use `body.model_fields_set` in `PUT /api/sets/{id}` so that an explicit `null` still un-groups (for `move_set`) but a missing key does not. Apply the same pattern to `system_prompt`, `mcp_system_context`, `thumbnail_source` and `thumbnail_diagram_id`, which have the same full-replace exposure.
3. **Tests.**
   - Change `TestUpdateSet` to assert `put_body["collection_id"] == "col-7"`.
   - Add a backend test: a PUT without `collection_id` keeps the set in its collection, and a PUT with `"collection_id": null` un-groups it.

## Workaround

Call `move_set` with the original `collection_id` straight after any `update_set`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `update_set` with only a name or description never changes `collection_id`.
- `move_set` with `collection_id: null` still un-groups a set.
- Both behaviours are covered by tests that use the real merge logic, not only a mocked response.
